items.title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips
items.summary: After the scandal around former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, lawmakers from both parties are backing measures to further restrict AI chip exports. AI chips are now a central piece of national security policy.

items.title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M for AI image sensors
items.summary: Indian startup Bharat Semi raised a 24 million dollar seed round to build programmable image sensors that capture, process, and run AI on a single chip. AI is moving to the edge, all the way into the sensor.

items.title: Apple's new study looks to improve AI health tools
items.summary: The Apple Health AI Usage Study runs with OpenEvidence, a clinical AI platform that answers from sources like the New England Journal of Medicine. Before trusting AI with health, someone has to measure whether it helps.

items.title: XYBench: Helping with the problem behind the question
items.summary: That's the XY problem: you want X, assume approach Y will work, and ask about Y. Like asking how to thicken frosting when your cupcakes are just too warm. A truly helpful assistant answers the problem behind the question.

items.title: Build a robot pick-and-place simulation with SimReady assets
items.summary: NVIDIA's walkthrough builds a pick-and-place task in Isaac Sim with a UR17G arm, a Robotiq gripper, and a beverage can. Good robot training starts with simulation assets that behave like the real thing.

items.title: How AI is helping care teams get patients the right care, sooner
items.summary: Hospitals hold decades of patient history in free text: physician notes, reports, and discharge summaries. The best clinical AI hands time back to care teams, not decisions.

items.title: llama.cpp v1.0.0: a stronger foundation for local AI
items.summary: llama.cpp runs large language models on almost any hardware, from laptops to enterprise servers, using quantization and portable C and C++ code. Stable APIs mean developers can build private, on-device AI with confidence.

items.title: AI agent startup LangChain hits $3B valuation
items.summary: LangChain raised a 300 million dollar Series C led by CapitalG, more than doubling the 1.25 billion dollar valuation it had about a year ago. In the agent era, the money is moving to tools that run and govern agents.

items.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across US airspace
items.summary: The FAA's 875 million dollar SMART system combines weather, flight paths, traffic flow, and staffing data to recommend routes and arrival order. AI as an advisor, with humans making the final call.

items.title: Claude's Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
items.summary: Claude Duet is Anthropic's agent for professionals and small business owners, in research preview for Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US. Agents get useful with lots of context, and that's also the tradeoff.

items.title: Export-banned Nvidia chips behind China's most powerful AI models, research claims
items.summary: Will DePue of the nonprofit Unemployment Labs analyzed open-weight models from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MiniMax, and Ant Group. Model weights may become evidence in the chip export fight.

items.title: ChatGPT Wallet lets OpenAI's Dots agents make purchases for you
items.summary: ChatGPT Wallet is rolling out to US ChatGPT Pro subscribers. Add a card, and your Dots agents can make purchases from your prompts. Agent payments are arriving, with humans still signing off.

items.title: Advancing science & engineering with Antigravity's /teamwork
items.summary: Google Research says /teamwork, a multi-agent system in Antigravity, worked with human experts on open problems in math, chemistry, systems software, and ML engineering. Lesson for agent builders: parallel attempts plus strict verification beats one long try.

items.title: Amazon has a plan to index the world's online shopping data
items.summary: According to Reuters, the project is called the World Product Graph. The goal is to keep shoppers, and AI shopping agents, from doing research elsewhere. When agents shop for us, whoever owns the product data wins.

items.title: Unbundling multimodal vision encoding
items.summary: Vision encoders bundle three choices: a visual prior from pretraining, dedicated vision capacity, and placing it before the language backbone. Give models dedicated room to see, and where it sits matters less.

items.title: Synthesis Smuggling: hiding inferred personal attributes in LLM outputs
items.summary: This paper describes a threat: a malicious model infers sensitive details about you from normal conversations. Text you share from an AI could carry more than you think.

items.title: Actor, judge, or teacher? Decision models in long-horizon agents
items.summary: Researchers tested models as actors that choose actions, and as judges that review a finished episode. Hindsight makes judging easier than acting.

items.title: Metal Sandbox: scheduling GPU coding agents on Apple silicon
items.summary: Agents that write Apple Metal kernels alternate between model calls, dev commands, and GPU runs, so GPU capacity sits unused. Smarter scheduling can squeeze far more from the hardware you already have.

items.title: LLMON: An LLM-native markup language, now in Granite 4.1
items.summary: An LLM's context mixes system prompts, chat turns, tool results, and documents, often in formats like JSON that weren't designed for language models. Better structure in the prompt could mean sturdier, safer small models.

items.title: Programming quantum circuit parameters with large language models
items.summary: Researchers asked a frozen, general-purpose LLM to write all the parameters for variational quantum circuits from text descriptions. LLMs help most when problems have structure, and answers can be verified.

source.name: arXiv (cs.LG), de Souza Farias et al.

items.title: LiveGeo: benchmarking geographic agents in evolving worlds
items.summary: Most benchmarks test agents on fixed snapshots. GeoWorld is a geographic environment, grounded in real-world structure, where conditions keep evolving over time. Real-world agents need to notice when their facts go stale.

items.title: LazyWeights: decode-on-demand edge LLMs
items.summary: Quantized formats spend the same bits on every weight code, even though some codes are far more common than others. Compression in hardware could bring bigger models to small devices.

items.title: Goal Encoding in LLMs
items.summary: In a coding task, researchers found the model's next sub-goal encoded in a small set of attention heads, and could even decode it into plain English. Interpretability is starting to reveal how models plan their next step.

items.title: Build once, run on any agent: a practical guide to agent skills
items.summary: An agent skill is a versioned folder built around a SKILL.md file that says when and how to do a repeatable task. Write your know-how down once, and every agent can reuse it.

items.title: Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
items.summary: The first Gemini glasses come from Warby Parker, starting at 395 dollars, and Gentle Monster, from 449. Samsung builds the hardware and Google handles the software. Without a screen, these glasses only work if you can trust the AI.

items.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen
items.summary: Meet Gemini 4 Hydrogen. While Carbon and Argon handle deep reasoning, Hydrogen is built for fast execution: writing code, running tests, and agent workflows. The trend: big models plan, fast models do the work.

items.title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
items.summary: Unlike left-to-right chatbots, diffusion models can remask and revise words. The researchers found token confidence doesn't reliably reveal errors, but hidden states do. Knowing when to revise can matter as much as generating well.

items.title: Classical Energies Learn to Reason 1,000x Faster than Looped Models
items.summary: Looped models are a popular way to teach AI to reason through puzzles, but they can be unstable, slow to train, and heavy on compute. Energy-based methods look promising, and easy puzzles may be weak reasoning benchmarks.

items.title: CoReMem: Cost-internalizing memory for successive coding tasks
items.summary: Coding agents work through a series of tasks on the same repository, writing memory before they know what's next. But memory costs effort to write and read. Good agent memory is small, specific, and proven useful.

items.title: Nvidia privately confirmed it could track chips to fight smuggling
items.summary: The Chip Security Act would require geotracking to verify the location of advanced AI chips, to stop them from being smuggled to China. AI chips are now treated as strategic assets, and location tracking is on the table.

items.title: CapLite: prompt-injection defense for small language model agents
items.summary: Several prompt-injection defenses ask the agent's own model to write a security policy. Across 15 open models, mostly 1.7 to 12 billion parameters, those policies let attacks through. For small agents, security should come from code, not the model.

items.title: Ballad: bandit-based LLM routing for automated heuristic discovery
items.summary: LLMs can now discover heuristics for hard optimization problems by repeatedly refining solutions. Mixing models wisely can beat paying for the biggest one.

items.title: AgentSSL: Can MLE agents leverage unlabeled data?
items.summary: Real projects often have little labeled data but lots of unlabeled data. This paper tests ML engineering agents in that setting. Agents can generate good ideas. Choosing the right one is harder.
